title: Ad Tracking & Targeted Advertising Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to stop ad tracking and prevent targeted advertising. Block behavioral ads and protect your privacy from data collection.
intro: Stop advertisers from tracking your every move online. This comprehensive checklist helps you disable targeted advertising, prevent cross-site tracking, and regain control of your digital privacy from behavioral advertising networks.

items.task: Disable third-party cookies in your browser
items.why: Third-party cookies are the primary mechanism for cross-site tracking and building advertising profiles about your browsing habits.
items.howTo: In Chrome: Settings > Privacy & Security > Cookies. Select 'Block third-party cookies'. In Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Enhanced Tracking Protection > Strict.

items.task: Enable Do Not Track headers
items.why: Sends a signal to websites requesting not to track you, though compliance is voluntary.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy & Security > Send 'Do Not Track' request. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Send websites a 'Do Not Track' signal.

items.task: Turn off personalized advertising in browser settings
items.why: Prevents browsers from using your browsing data to show targeted ads and sharing data with advertisers.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy & Security > Ad privacy > Ad topics, Site-suggested ads, Ad measurement (turn all off). Edge: Settings > Privacy > Ad blocking.

items.task: Install a comprehensive ad blocker extension
items.why: Blocks tracking scripts, advertising networks, and prevents data collection from ad-serving domains.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin from your browser's extension store. Enable additional filter lists like EasyPrivacy for enhanced tracking protection.

items.task: Use private/incognito browsing for sensitive activities
items.why: Prevents local storage of cookies and browsing history that could be used for ad targeting.
items.howTo: Use Ctrl+Shift+N (Chrome) or Ctrl+Shift+P (Firefox) for private windows. Consider a privacy-focused browser for enhanced privacy protection.

items.task: Regularly clear cookies, cache, and browsing data
items.why: Removes stored tracking data and resets advertising profiles built from your browsing history.
items.howTo: Chrome: Ctrl+Shift+Delete, select 'All time' and check cookies, cached images, browsing history. Set up automatic clearing if available.

items.task: Disable Google ad personalization
items.why: Google uses data from search, YouTube, Gmail, and partner sites to create detailed advertising profiles for targeted ads.
items.howTo: Visit myaccount.google.com/data-and-privacy > Ad personalization. Turn off 'Ad Personalization' and delete your advertising ID.

items.task: Opt out of Facebook ad tracking and targeting
items.why: Facebook tracks users across websites and apps to serve highly targeted ads based on detailed behavioral profiles.
items.howTo: Facebook Settings > Ads > Ad Settings. Turn off ads based on data from partners, ads based on your activity on Facebook, and ads that include your social actions.

items.task: Disable Microsoft advertising personalization
items.why: Microsoft collects data from Bing, Windows, and partner sites for targeted advertising in their network.
items.howTo: Visit account.microsoft.com/privacy/ad-settings. Turn off 'See personalized ads in your browser' and 'See personalized ads wherever you use your Microsoft account'.

items.task: Turn off Amazon advertising personalization
items.why: Amazon uses purchase history and browsing data to create advertising profiles used across their ecosystem and partner sites.
items.howTo: Amazon account > Your Account > Advertising preferences. Turn off 'Personalized ads on Amazon' and 'Ads from Amazon on other sites'.

items.task: Disable Twitter ad personalization and data sharing
items.why: Twitter tracks engagement and interests to serve targeted ads and shares data with advertising partners.
items.howTo: Twitter Settings > Privacy and Safety > Ads preferences. Turn off 'Personalized ads' and 'Ads based on your identity from advertising partners'.

items.task: Reset or disable advertising ID on mobile devices
items.why: Advertising IDs allow apps to track you across different applications and serve targeted ads based on your mobile behavior.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Apple Advertising > Personalized Ads (off). Android: Settings > Privacy > Ads > Reset advertising ID or Opt out of Ads Personalization.

items.task: Limit app tracking permissions
items.why: Apps can track your behavior across other apps and websites to build detailed profiles for advertising purposes.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking > Allow Apps to Request to Track (off). Review individual app permissions. Android: Check app permissions in Settings > Apps.

items.task: Use DNS filtering to block tracking domains
items.why: DNS-level blocking prevents connections to known advertising and tracking domains before they can load.
items.howTo: Configure router or device DNS to use privacy-focused services like Quad9 (9.9.9.9) or Cloudflare for Families (1.1.1.3) that block malware and tracking.

items.task: Use VPN with built-in ad and tracker blocking
items.why: VPNs can mask your IP address and some include features to block advertising domains and tracking scripts.
items.howTo: Choose a VPN service that includes ad/tracker blocking features. Enable these features in the VPN app settings for additional protection.

items.task: Review and update privacy settings across all devices
items.why: Default settings often favor data collection for advertising. Regular reviews ensure new tracking features are disabled.
items.howTo: Schedule monthly reviews of privacy settings on phones, computers, smart TVs, and other connected devices. Disable data sharing and personalization options.

items.task: Use Network Advertising Initiative (NAI) opt-out tool
items.why: Opts you out of behavioral advertising from hundreds of participating advertising networks and data brokers.
items.howTo: Visit optout.networkadvertising.org and click 'Opt Out of All' to disable interest-based advertising from NAI members.

items.task: Use Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) opt-out tools
items.why: Provides opt-out mechanisms for interest-based advertising across web and mobile environments.
items.howTo: Visit optout.aboutads.info for web opt-outs and youradchoices.com/appchoices for mobile app advertising opt-outs.

items.task: Opt out from major data brokers individually
items.why: Data brokers collect and sell personal information to advertisers. Opting out reduces available data for targeted advertising.
items.howTo: Visit opt-out pages for major brokers like Acxiom, Epsilon, Experian, LexisNexis. Each has different processes, typically requiring name, address verification.

items.task: Opt out of location-based advertising services
items.why: Location data enables highly targeted advertising based on places you visit and your daily patterns.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > Location-Based Apple Ads (off). Android: Google Settings > Ads > Opt out of location-based ads.

items.task: Enable email tracking protection
items.why: Email tracking pixels allow advertisers to know when you open emails and can trigger retargeting campaigns.
items.howTo: Apple Mail: Mail settings > Privacy Protection (on). Outlook: File > Options > Trust Center > Automatic Download > Don't download pictures automatically.

pro_tips: Use multiple browsers: Keep one for general browsing with strong privacy settings and another for sites requiring cookies and tracking.
Check privacy policies before using new apps or services - look for data sharing with advertising partners and opt-out mechanisms.
Consider using a privacy-focused browser or other privacy-focused browsers that block tracking by default instead of relying on browser extensions.
Set up a separate email address for shopping and services to limit the personal data connected to your main email for advertising purposes.
Regularly audit your social media privacy settings as platforms frequently update their advertising and data sharing policies.
